source.what: FlowSpace contact page (flowspace.framer.website/contact): a full-bleed black hero split into a 64px 'Let's connect' invitation with four icon contact rows on the left and an inline four-field enquiry form on the right, followed by a light FAQ band pairing a two-line heading with a six-row accordion, then a two-row counter-scrolling testimonial marquee of white quote cards, then the black footer. The only FlowSpace page whose hero is dark and whose body is light, and the only one carrying an accordion.
source.method: Node + puppeteer-core driving local Chromium (ms-playwright build). Loaded at 1440x900, 834x1112, 390x844; entrance animations sampled at 100ms intervals from first paint to read durations, delays, easings and per-property keyframes before they finished; marquee animations read live (not finished) so their travel distance and direction could be measured; FAQ rows enumerated in their open and closed states; full-page and fold stills per width. Computed-style probes on the H1, section headings, contact rows, form labels, the four field wrappers, the select, the submit control, the FAQ rows and answer, the testimonial cards, ratings, quotes, avatars and the footer. Behaviour probes: viewport changes across the three widths with re-measured H1 size and field boxes.
gaps: The FAQ was not clicked. Its six rows were enumerated in their resting states (the first open at 110px, the rest closed at 54px except a two-line question at 77px) and the open/closed transition was not triggered or timed. Whether the rows animate their height, fade the answer, or snap is unverified.

The closing 10s opacity reveal on the first FAQ answer is recorded from the animation timeline (opacity 0.001 to 1, 10000ms, 5000ms delay, cubic-bezier(0.12,0.23,0.37,1)) but its trigger is unresolved: it is registered on load and had not visibly completed during sampling. It is the same animation that appeared unexplained on the sibling home, locations and property rubrics, and this page is where its target — the first FAQ answer — was identified.

Marquee travel was measured as +-2754px in a 1440x1440 viewport at 110160ms per pass with linear easing, giving the two rows opposite directions. The exact modulus that makes the loop seamless (the repeated card count) was not resolved, and the row directions were inferred from the two sign-opposed translateX keyframe pairs rather than from watching a full cycle.
Hover and focus states were not probed on this page: the submit pill, the FAQ rows' cursor affordance, the contact rows and the nav were not exercised.

The FAQ chevron swaps between a plus glyph on closed rows and a multiplication-style cross on the open row. Both render, but whether they are two icons swapped or one rotated glyph was not determined.

The testimonial avatars are demo portraits; their image set was not inventoried. Cards are clipped at both viewport edges by the marquee, so the total card count in the loop is not visible in any single still.

The form is a demo: four select options, no submission endpoint exercised, and no validation or error states captured. The submit pill has a 48px radius against the template's usual 24px, which is recorded as measured rather than as a deliberate system choice.

The contact rows carry four entries (email, phone, hours, social handle) while the footer repeats only the first three; whether the social handle is intentionally footer-omitted or simply not repeated was not resolved.
DM Sans and Inter load with the document but render no visible text; only Plus Jakarta Sans was observed.
Wrapper nodes computing the default link blue rgb(0,0,238) appear here as on the sibling pages and are treated as not part of the design.
The H1 measures 64px at 1440w and 56px at 834w, but the breakpoint at which it steps down was not located.
Template content is placeholder: demo quotes attributed to four recurring demo names, hello@yourcoworking.com and +33 6 12 34 56 78.
Validation is partial: discrimination was measured against the three sibling FlowSpace page rubrics, but a sensitivity pass, an invariance pass and a blind re-score are not recorded on this page.
Production use requires human sign-off on this frozen file.
source.notes: Fourth of four FlowSpace page rubrics, after flowspace_home_v1, flowspace_property_single_v1 and flowspace_locations_v1. This page inverts the template's default polarity: its hero is the black full-bleed band that the other pages use only for the CTA panel and footer, and its body is the light band. It is also the only FlowSpace page with an accordion, and the only one running two counter-scrolling marquees. The 64px H1 is the largest type in the template, one step above the 40px used on the sibling pages.

parts.name: Black hero with the form inline in its right half
parts.description: The page opens on a full-bleed black band 1440x800 and splits it into a 508px invitation column and a 508px form column with 64px between them, both inside the 1120px container. The form is not a card: there is no white panel, no border and no shadow, so the translucent grey field wrappers sit directly on black and the only white mass in the hero is the full-width submit pill. This inverts the template's usual polarity, where the dark element is a CTA panel at the foot of a light page.
parts.entry_test: Box the form in a white card and the hero becomes the property page's sticky rail, not this page. Leaving the fields loose on black is what makes the hero read as one continuous dark surface with a white button as its single punctuation, and it is the page's opening identity.

parts.name: Counter-scrolling testimonial marquee
parts.description: The page's social proof is two full-bleed rows of white quote cards running in opposite directions. Each row is a list 5492px wide inside a 1440px viewport, animated linearly over 110160ms; the measured keyframes translate one list from 0 to -2754px and the other from 0 to +2754px, so the rows cross while the cards are clipped at both viewport edges. The band is 698px tall and 416px of that is the two rows.
parts.entry_test: Freeze the rows into a static grid and the page loses the only thing that distinguishes its social proof from the home page's. Two lists drifting opposite ways past the viewport edge is the page's closing gesture, and the clipping is what signals that the set continues beyond the screen.

parts.name: White-row accordion
parts.description: The FAQ is a stack of six white rounded rows on the light canvas, each 540px wide with an 8px radius and 16px padding, holding a 16px weight-500 question and a glyph pinned at the right edge. Exactly one row is open on load and it is taller: the measured open row is 110px against 54px for a closed one, the extra 56px carrying a 14px answer in secondary ink. The rows carry no dividers and no borders; the white fill against the near-white canvas plus the 16px gap between rows is the whole separation.
parts.entry_test: Strip the white fills and the six questions become a plain list with plus signs. The filled row is what makes each question a discrete thing you can open, and the single expanded row is what shows the pattern without needing a user action to demonstrate it.

parts.recipe: Stack six rows with a 16px gap. Each row: background #fff, radius 8px, padding 16px, a flex row with the 16px/500 question at the left and a small glyph at the right. Render the answer inside the open row only, at 14px in rgba(31,31,31,0.8), about 56px below the question. Open the first row by default. Use a plus glyph on closed rows and a cross or rotated glyph on the open one.

parts.name: Two-word blur-settle headline
parts.description: The 64px headline resolves rather than appears: 'Let's' and 'connect' are separate spans, each animating opacity from 0.001 and a filter blur from 4px to 0 over 1100ms on cubic-bezier(0.12,0.23,0.17,0.98), the second word 100ms behind the first. The 64px size makes this the template's largest application of the move, and the two-word split gives it a visible stagger that the longer headlines on the sibling pages do not.
parts.entry_test: Drop the blur and the page's opening beat loses its only softness — this page leads with the largest type in the template, and the resolve is what stops 64px black-on-black from simply snapping on. It is the same settle move the home page runs, scaled up.
parts.recipe: Split the H1 into one span per word. Animate each span from opacity 0.001 and filter blur(4px) to opacity 1 and blur(0), 1100ms on cubic-bezier(0.12,0.23,0.17,0.98), with the second span delayed 100ms. Keep the H1's own tracking at -2.56px so the words still read as one line.

limitations: The FAQ was never clicked. Rows were enumerated in their resting states (first open at 110px, five closed at 54px, one 77px because its question wraps) and the open/closed transition was not triggered or timed. Whether rows animate their height, fade the answer, or snap is unverified.

The 10s opacity reveal on the first FAQ answer was read from the animation timeline but its trigger is unresolved: it is registered on load with a 5000ms delay, and at the sampling point 6.7s in it had not visibly completed. This page is where the animation's target was finally identified, but the mechanism that starts it is still unknown.

Marquee travel was measured as +-2754px per pass over 110160ms from the keyframes, and the two rows' opposite directions were inferred from the sign of those translateX pairs rather than from watching a full cycle. The modulus that makes the loop seamless was not resolved, and the total card count in each loop is not visible in any single still because cards clip at both viewport edges.
Hover and focus states were not probed on this page: the submit pill, the FAQ rows, the contact rows and the nav were not exercised.
The FAQ glyph differs between rows: plus on closed and a multiplication-style cross on the open one. Both render, but whether they are two swapped icons or one rotated glyph was not determined.
The H1 measures 64px at 1440w and 56px at 834w; the breakpoint where it steps down was not located.
The contact block carries four values while the footer repeats only three (the social handle is omitted); whether that omission is deliberate was not resolved.

The submit pill computes a 48px radius against the template's usual 24px on the sibling pages. That is recorded as measured; whether it is a deliberate variant or an artefact of the pill being 48px tall was not determined.
The form is a demo: four select options, no submission endpoint exercised, and no validation, error or success states captured.
The testimonial avatars are demo portraits and their image set was not inventoried; only their circular framing and approximate size are recorded.
DM Sans and Inter load with the document but render no visible text; only Plus Jakarta Sans was observed.
Wrapper nodes computing the default link blue rgb(0,0,238) appear here as on the sibling pages and are treated as not part of the design.
Template content is placeholder: four demo quotes attributed to four recurring demo names, demo portraits, hello@yourcoworking.com and +33 6 12 34 56 78.
Validation is partial: discrimination was measured against the three sibling FlowSpace page rubrics, but a sensitivity pass, an invariance pass and a blind re-score are not recorded here.
Production use requires human sign-off on this frozen file.
